title: STALEMATE! STALEMATE! STALEMATE!
reviewNotes: Four branches, 17 exact positions from full five-piece board. Ne2, Kc4 and Nd4 prepare the rook sacrifice Nxc6+ ...Kb6. Three actual stalemates contrasted with c8=R; exact winning underpromotion endpoint is not called immediate mate.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to [music] win from this position. You see, white does have a pawn that can promote to a queen, but promoting would be a massive mistake. After rook to C3 with a check, the king will have to move and the queen will fall. But of course, white can play knight to E2 and now use the knight to defend the crucial C3 square. It seems like the promotion is inevitable, but black plays a seemingly mysterious move, king to A5. This doesn't change anything, right? We can just get the queen and be completely winning. As it turns out, black can play rook to C3 check. And now, if the knight takes, this is going to be a stalemate. The king has no legal moves, but it's not checked, so the game is a draw. But wait, it doesn't seem too hard for white to get out of this trap. After a move like king to C4, the rook is now under attack and it has to move and there is going to be no stalemate for black. But black doesn't resign and instead, he plays rook to D6. What could possibly be the idea here? Surely we can just promote now. But you see, you can never lower your guard in chess. Rook to C6, another brilliant counter shot. Of course, this forks the king and queen, but if the queen takes, this is going to be yet another stalemate. But it seems like white can play knight to D4, defend that square and now surely there is no other way to prevent the promotion, right? Well, not exactly. Black plays rook to C6 anyway. This doesn't seem to make any sense. The knight of course captures, otherwise the pawn would be lost. But now black follows up with king to B6. Now the pawn and the knight are under attack, but of course, we can finally promote to a queen. Except, we cannot. This is yet again another stalemate. Incredibly, black [music] still kicks. But, of course, we are under no obligation to promote to a queen. So, white will promote to a rook instead. There is no stalemate, and with a knight and a rook, it is going to be a simple win for white. If you love incredible chess, follow for more.
